transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see us today?

I’ve gotten into this habit of making myself throw up after I eat, and I can’t seem to stop doing it even though I know it’s not right. I'm just really embarrassed to even admit it, but I know I need some help.
Do you often feel anxious or worried about your weight or body shape, and does this feeling influence your decision to make yourself throw up after eating?

Yes, I do. Any time I feel my work coveralls getting tight or catch my reflection in the shop glass, I panic and feel like a total failure. That intense fear of gaining weight is exactly what drives me to force myself to throw up, especially after a heavy meal, just so I can feel empty and keep the weight off.
Do you often eat an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most people would eat in a similar period, and then feel a lack of control during these episodes?

Yes, on busy nights after work I'll stand at the kitchen counter and plow through half a pizza, chips, and leftovers in twenty minutes, which is way more than my family eats. Once I start, it's like a switch flips and my hands keep shoving food in my mouth even though my head is screaming at me to stop. I just can't seem to slow down until I feel physically sick.
Can you tell me how often you have these episodes of eating a large amount of food followed by making yourself throw up, and have you noticed any significant fluctuations in your weight over time?

This happens pretty much every week, with me binging on several nights when I get home and forcing myself to throw up at least a couple of times. My weight hasn't actually swung up or down by a huge amount, but I obsessively watch the scale and completely panic if it creeps up by even half a pound.
Can you estimate how often you make yourself throw up in relation to the times you binge eat, is it after almost every binge or only sometimes?

I don't do it every single time, but it's definitely a regular weekly habit now. I usually binge several nights a week when I get home stressed from the shop, and I'll force myself to throw up at least a couple of those times. So it's not after every single binge, but it happens pretty much every week.
Can you tell me more about the times when you binge eat but do not make yourself throw up, what happens during those instances and how do you feel afterwards?

I'm not quite sure, as I haven't really thought about it that way. Even on the nights when I don't throw up, I still feel incredibly guilty and panicked about gaining weight, but I don't really have a different routine or distinct feelings for those times. I usually just end up lying in bed feeling miserable and hating myself.
Do you also use other methods to compensate for the calories consumed during binge eating, such as excessive exercise, fasting, or using laxatives, in addition to making yourself throw up?

No, I don't do any of those things. I've never used laxatives, taken diet pills, or tried fasting and excessive workouts. Forcing myself to throw up is really the only way I try to get rid of the food.

Can you describe the frequency and regularity of your self-induced vomiting in relation to your menstrual cycle, if you're female, or any other physical effects you've noticed as a result of this behavior?

I haven't really noticed any connection between making myself throw up and my menstrual cycle. I'm not sure about other specific physical effects, but I've just been feeling really worn down and dragging at work lately.
